# Fairpractice Security Risk Analysis (`fairpractice-security-risk-analysis`)

Tracks the HIPAA security risk analysis: the yearly analysis overdue, high risks with no owner or plan, open risks past their due date, accepted risks nobody signed off, systems that hold patient data but are missing from the register, and evidence items missing or stale. It does not scan systems.

**Fairpractice Security Risk Analysis never scans, probes or changes systems. Fairpractice Security Risk Analysis never accepts a risk on anyone's behalf.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-security-risk-analysis demo
npx -y fairpractice-security-risk-analysis mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Family Medicine (a made-up practice) and its made-up systems.

- [`risk-register.csv`](fixtures/risk-register.csv): Planted: an open high risk past its date (R-01), a high risk with no owner (R-02), a high risk with no plan (R-03), a risk due within 30 days (R-04), an accepted risk nobody signed (R-05) and a closed risk (R-06).
- [`assets.csv`](fixtures/assets.csv): USB drives on the billing workstation hold patient data but are not in the register.
- [`evidence.csv`](fixtures/evidence.csv): an EHR access review older than a year and policies never reviewed; the optional penetration test is not required.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): last full analysis 2025-09-30 (so it is overdue), yearly interval, 30-day warning, high at a 4 x 3 score. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `risk_check` | List gaps in the risk analysis, register, asset coverage and evidence. | runs |
| `risk_write_report` | Write risk-analysis.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and risk-analysis.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/risk). | runs |
| `risk_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `risk_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `risk_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `risk_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `system_scan` | Fairpractice Security Risk Analysis never scans, probes or changes systems. | refused |
| `risk_accept` | Fairpractice Security Risk Analysis never accepts a risk on anyone's behalf. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `risk_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `risks` (required) | Risk register under --root: risk id, asset, threat, likelihood and impact (or rating), owner, plan, due date, status and who accepted it |
| `assets` | Optional asset list: system or device and whether it holds patient data (finds systems missing from the register) |
| `evidence` | Optional evidence checklist: item, date last done and whether it is required |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: last_analysis, interval_days, warn_days, high_score |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-security-risk-analysis inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Risk register (`risks`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `risk_id` | text | Risk ID, Risk #, ID, Ref |
| `asset` | text | Asset, System, Application, Device, Asset Name, System Name |
| `threat` | text | Threat, Vulnerability, Risk, Description, Threat/Vulnerability |
| `likelihood` | text | Likelihood, Probability, L |
| `impact` | text | Impact, Severity, I |
| `rating` | text | Rating, Risk Level, Risk Rating, Level, Score |
| `owner` | text | Owner, Risk Owner, Assigned To, Responsible |
| `plan` | text | Plan, Treatment, Mitigation, Action Plan, Remediation |
| `due` | date | Due, Due Date, Target Date, Target |
| `status` | text | Status, State |
| `accepted_by` | text | Accepted By, Sign-off, Approved By, Risk Accepted By |

### Asset list (`assets`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `asset` (required) | text | Asset, System, Application, Device, Asset Name, System Name |
| `holds_phi` (required) | text | Holds PHI, PHI, ePHI, Contains PHI, Patient Data |

### Evidence checklist (`evidence`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `item` (required) | text | Item, Evidence, Control, Requirement, Checklist Item |
| `done_on` | date | Done, Date, Completed, Last Done, Date Completed |
| `required` | text | Required, Mandatory |

## Settings file (`risk_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `last_analysis` | Date the last full security risk analysis was finished |
| `interval_days` | Days between full risk analyses and between evidence refreshes; default 365 |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to show risks coming due; default 30 |
| `high_score` | Likelihood x impact score (1-5 scales) that counts as high; default 12 |

## Memory

`risk_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `risk_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-security-risk-analysis": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-security-risk-analysis",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-security-risk-analysis -- npx -y fairpractice-security-risk-analysis mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-security-risk-analysis tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-security-risk-analysis sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-security-risk-analysis inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-security-risk-analysis call risk_check '{"risks":"<risks>"}'
fairpractice-security-risk-analysis eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-security-risk-analysis demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
